gaps.text: In-line measurement of Turbidity / optical density of the stream with in-line turbidity (optical density) sensor
In-line measurement of Stream temperature with process temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Two blocks, NIR reflection and MIR-ATR, would be fused at the variable level with block scaling, because variables from different methods are not equivalent. Both probes must see the same material at the same time, which in a flowing stream means a combined probe or closely co-located ports with acquisition normalised to a common time step. Each block keeps its own calibration and diagnostics, and the fused model must beat the best single method on held-out runs before the second instrument is justified.)
No supplied source gives an accuracy, detection limit or response time for protein measurement in whey, or names a validated laboratory reference method for whey protein.

items.finding: The review states that temperature sensitivity of OH bands is a severe drawback for aqueous NIR and MIR measurements, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform the assessment by highlighting the need to monitor or control stream temperature and to test temperature effects on the NIR/MIR signal.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a review in biopharmaceutical downstream processing, not dairy whey, and it refers to tempered sample holders rather than an in-line process temperature sensor.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E01 ¶12

items.finding: The review recommends evaluating each dataset's contribution and complementarity before fusing data from multiple sources.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform a staged comparison of NIR reflection and MIR-ATR blocks, checking whether each adds information before committing to a fused model.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a review of PAT data fusion, not a whey study, and it does not address block scaling or co-located probes in a flowing dairy stream.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E03 ¶82

items.finding: The review notes that instrument complementarity was not sufficient to improve performance for several CQAs in a Raman and FT-IR food analytical study.
items.how_it_applies: This is a reason to require the fused NIR/MIR model to outperform the best single method on held-out runs before adding the second instrument.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited example used Raman and FT-IR on food matrices, not NIR reflection and MIR-ATR on whey, so the negative result may not transfer.

citation.quote: In some situations, instrument complementarity (not data complementarity) was not sufficient to improve the performance of predictive several CQAs, as shown by a Raman and FT-IR data based food analytical study [73].
citation.label: E03 ¶36
